slides.title: Interchanging between exponential and log form

transcription.tex: \(\log_a n=x\) (said “log base \(a\) of \(n\)”) is equivalent to \(a^x=n\).\par The logarithm outputs the missing power. Here \(a>0\), \(a\ne1\) and \(n>0\).
Here are two methods of interchanging between these forms. Pick your favourite!
The base of the logarithm must match the base of the exponential.\par \(\log_2 8\) asks: “2 to what power gives 8?”
Imagine inserting the output of the logarithm just after its base. Click the button to move the missing power.

transcription.printTex: Animation available on the online slide.

transcription.tex: Method 2: Do the same operation to each side
Since KS3, you have used the same operation on each side of an equation to undo whatever you want to remove.\par For example, subtract 2 from each side:\par \(3x+2=11\quad\Rightarrow\quad3x=9\).
“Log base \(a\)” and “\(a\) to the power of” undo each other: they are inverse functions.

sourceAnimationMapping.meaning: Output moves beside the base as an exponent; log form becomes equivalent exponential form.
